best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
As we look back from August 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a season cut dramatically short by the pandemic, yet the productions that did premiere before the shutdown demonstrated remarkable artistic ambition and social relevance. Despite the truncated season, these works continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike, maintaining an impressive average score of 74 out of 100.

Leading the critical rankings is "A Soldier's Play," Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally received its long-overdue Broadway debut. Critics consistently praise the production's powerful examination of racial tension within a World War II Army unit, noting how the work's themes remain urgently relevant decades after it was written. The stellar ensemble cast brings nuance and intensity to Fuller's complex characters, making this revival feel both historically grounded and strikingly contemporary.

Ivo van Hove's reimagining of "West Side Story" proves to be the season's most polarizing production, with critics sharply divided over its radical approach to the beloved musical. While some reviewers celebrate the director's bold vision and innovative use of video design, others question whether the experimental staging serves or obscures the classic material. Meanwhile, Bess Wohl's "Grand Horizons" offers lighter fare with its Neil Simon-esque exploration of late-life divorce, earning praise particularly for its veteran cast.

These productions from early 2020 capture a brief moment before Broadway went dark for an unprecedented period. Whether you're interested in hard-hitting drama, experimental reinventions of classics, or character-driven comedy, exploring the top-rated shows from this unique season offers insight into both theatrical excellence and a pivotal moment in Broadway history.

From verbatim FBI transcripts in "Is This a Room" to the warmly nostalgic one-person storytelling of "Lackawanna Blues," from the pop concert energy of "SIX" to the long-overdue Broadway debut of Alice Childress' "Trouble in Mind," these shows represent theater at its most varied and vital. Whether you're drawn to experimental documentary theater, lavish musical revivals, or intimate dramas, the top-rated shows from 2021's historic Broadway season offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:

This year's strong showing for dramatic works reflects Broadway's renewed commitment to serious plays alongside its musical offerings.
